notes:
Summary: Crestline is a mid-tier digital-banking platform (customer-facing chat + personalization + fraud/rerank) evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production inference. Procurement stage: SLA + throughput guarantees are gating the deal.

Context / ask: They need a negotiated throughput guarantee that maps to their peak marketing and fraud workloads. Primary ask is a committed minimum sustained tokens/sec and rules for concurrency caps + burst. Also negotiating SLOs (p95/p99) for short-form responses and for long generation flows.

Key numbers discussed (draft):
- Target sustained min throughput: 8,000 tokens/sec for their primary model (LlamaX-34B quantized) across tenant pool.
- Planned concurrency cap: 120 active sessions (concurrent chat users) mapped to reserved pool.
- Burst policy: allow 200 concurrent sessions for up to 10s windows with token-rate throttling; bursts billed at pro-rated rate unless safety margin used.
- Reserved GPU plan: initial commit 8 x A100 80GB equiv (can be H100 depending on procurement) with autoscale burst to +2 GPUs on short notice (financial penalty for frequent bursts).
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 250ms for generation segments <= 256 tokens, p99 < 500ms; end-to-end chat pipeline (prompt + retrieval + gen) p95 < 400ms target.

POC findings (Sophie SE ran perf tests 2026-02-25):
- Synthetic conversational trace (median prompt length 42 tokens) sustained ~9k tokens/sec on 8 GPUs when batching and KV-cache enabled.
- Under high short-turn load with prefix cache, observed effective token/sec spike to ~18k for 30s windows; sustained tail performance drops if concurrency unbounded.
- Reranker (mini-batch) throughput predicted 15k qps for embedding-rerank path with dedicated CPU workers + 2 GPUs for scoring.

Security / compliance notes:
- Crestline requires SOC2 + SSO/SAML, KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and audit logs for all inference requests. Data residency: US only (must pin to us-east-1).
- Security is reviewing the Private control plane docs; they may request an on-prem package for very sensitive models later.

Negotiation points open:
- Exact SLA language for sustained min tokens/sec (how measured: 5-minute rolling avg? 1-minute?) — Crestline prefers 5-min sustained.
- Concurrency accounting: whether long-poll websocket sessions count as active concurrently for cap.
- Burst billing: flat per-GPU invoice vs. pro-rated per-second token billing during bursts.
- Penalty/credits for missing SLOs (service credits tier) and whether partial credits apply per model route.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-20: Intro AE call (Ravi) — identified use cases and security constraints.
- 2026-02-11: Deep-dive with infra + security (Fireflies ff-2026-02-11-0291).
- 2026-02-25: SE perf run + preliminary sizing (report attached to drive).

Quotes / call snippets: "We can accept a burst buffer if there is a clear billing model — we need predictable monthly costs more than unlimited bursts." — Crestline VP Eng.
"5-minute rolling average for tokens/sec is reasonable; 1-minute creates too much volatility." — Sophie (SE, Redwood).

Open artifacts requested from Crestline:
- Synthetic production traces (we have one sample; need 7 days of anonymized traces).
- Confirmation of model quantization/profile (they plan 4-bit POUR quantization).

Risks: procurement timeline slipping if legal insists on custom SLA wording; security may require Private deployment if KMS integration isn't supported in Dedicated plan per their policy.

Next steps (actionable):
- SE/SRE sizing workshop 2026-03-18 to finalize GPU count and burst tolerances (owner: Sophie).
- AE to submit draft throughput addendum by 2026-03-10 (owner: Ravi).
- Crestline to share 7-day anonymized traces by 2026-03-12 (owner: Crestline infra).
